subject: How can I fill points with black / white depending on the sign of the data?

messages.author: 006490a058657fd7
messages.subject: How can I fill points with black / white depending on the sign of the data?
parts:
I am trying to figure out a nice way to plot some sensitivity
statistics (vector 'a', below) that have both positive and negative
values. Because of their distribution, it would be more clear to
present them on a log-scale, e.g. the log(abs()).

I would like to use either filled(+) or empty(-) circles to indicate
sign, but am not sure how to do this without making separate calls to
geom_point*() and I would like to learn if there is a way to do this
with a single call.

Here is some example data:

a <- c(-100, 1, -4, 30)

and a plot

ggplot() + geom_pointrange(aes(1:4, log(abs(a)),
ymin=0,
ymax=log(abs(a))),
shape = 21, fill =
'black')

but I would like to replace 'black' with "ifelse(a<0,'white','black')"

Thanks,

David

messages.subject: Re: How can I fill points with black / white depending on the sign of the data?
parts:
On 11-01-04 03:36 PM, David L wrote:
> I am trying to figure out a nice way to plot some sensitivity
> statistics (vector 'a', below) that have both positive and negative
> values. Because of their distribution, it would be more clear to
> present them on a log-scale, e.g. the log(abs()).
>
> I would like to use either filled(+) or empty(-) circles to indicate
> sign, but am not sure how to do this without making separate calls to
> geom_point*() and I would like to learn if there is a way to do this
> with a single call.

d <- data.frame(x=1:4,a)
ggplot(d) +
geom_pointrange(aes(x=x, y=log(abs(a)),
ymin=0,ymax=log(abs(a)),
fill=factor(a<0),
shape=21))+
scale_fill_manual(value=c("black","white"))
